Prusa CORE One+ INDX conversion with the Gen 2 upgrade

One continuous guide that merges the INDX conversion guide, the CORE One+ Gen 2 upgrade guide and the companion article that tells you when to switch between them. 349 steps and article sections in assembly order, with the 725 most useful of 1167 community comments. Compiled from help.prusa3d.com on 7 Oct 2026.

Roadmap

INDXCh. 1–2, 3.1–3.10Introduction, disassembly, front bed spacers
Article“Securing the bed spacer - right, additional information”Unplug X/Y motors; remove left top cover and left metal panel
INDX3.11–3.19Rear bed spacer and offset sensor (offset-sensor screw only a few turns in)
Gen 24.4–4.8Replace the expansion joints; place the 10 mm heatbed spacer
INDX3.20–3.39, 4.1–4.3Heatbed back in (screws 2 turns only), cables, bed stop; release belts
Article“Additional information and removing the belts”Remove right top cover and right panel; lubricate tensioner screws
Gen 23.4–3.38New pulleys and finer-pitch belts (skip the Bowden-guide step, Gen 2 3.18)
INDX4.4–4.52Gantry alignment, INDX toolhead, head cable, filament sensors (skip the tensioner-lube step, INDX 4.12)
Article“Mounting the side panels, PTFE and right cover”Refit both top see-through covers (leave out the left top-middle rivet, and the right one too on 8-tool)
INDX4.53–4.71, 5.1–5.17PTFE tubes, side handle, nozzle cleaner, dock fan cable
Gen 24.11–4.20Align the expansion joints and tighten the heatbed
Article“Mounting the left cover, covering the electronics”Tighten the offset sensor; reconnect X/Y motors; left panel (3 rivets)
INDX5.18–5.104Electronics covers, spool holders, tool dock, top cover, nozzles
INDX + Gen 2INDX Ch. 6, Gen 2 5.6Firmware, set up the printer, Gen 2 edition change (right after INDX 6.7), wizard
INDX INDX conversion guide GEN 2 Gen 2 upgrade guide ARTICLE Companion article ↗ opens the original step online

Read first: what the official docs don't say clearly

  • The X/Y motors stay unplugged from the first article section until the last one (after the heatbed alignment). Several commenters suggest plugging them back in earlier, around INDX 4.35. That isn't in the official instructions; if you do it, just confirm them in the final article section.
  • Three things stay loose until the Gen 2 heatbed alignment (Gen 2 4.11–4.20): the heatbed screws (two turns only in INDX 3.25), the expansion joints' final alignment, and the offset-sensor screw (a few turns in INDX 3.17).
  • Use the new 10 mm heatbed spacer (Gen 2 4.8), not the old 8 mm one that INDX 3.21 lists.
  • Skip INDX 4.12 (tensioner lube is already done) and Gen 2 3.18 (INDX doesn't use the Bowden-guide).
  • Gen 2 edition change: the Gen 2 guide requires setting the printer edition to Gen 2 because of the new belt pitch. The companion article never mentions it. It's included right after INDX 6.7, with a heads-up on that step itself, because that's where you pick the printer model.
  • Many commenters found it easier to take both side panels off early and leave them off until needed. Bring M3x12 screws for the head cable clip (INDX 4.32), and pre-thread self-tapping holes in printed parts throughout chapter 5.

Yellow Compiler's note boxes are additions made while merging the guides. They are not Prusa's text, and neither are the roadmap, this card, or the phase and section labels. Step and article text is copied from the official pages; comments are from the community. Comments are filtered to tips, problems and fixes, corrections and Prusa staff answers. Faded comments are shown only as context for a useful reply.

ARTICLE

About this combination (article introduction)

↗

If you received your Prusa CORE One INDX conversion kit with the Prusa CORE One+ Gen 2 upgrade, or bought the Gen 2 upgrade separately and want to install both at the same time, this article will help you with the process. Read the instructions and information in this article thoroughly.

If you received the CORE One+ GEN 2 upgrade as part of your Prusa INDX conversion kit, note that all the GEN 2 upgrade parts (belts, Pulleys, spacers, fasteners, etc.) are included in the UPGRADE box.

There are some differences between the Prusa CORE One INDX and the Prusa CORE One+ Gen 2 guides. We will inform you when to switch to each guide with a handy link to the corresponding step.
In both guides, you will be alerted when you should switch back to this article.

A. Introduction & disassemblyINDX Ch. 1–2, 3.1–3.10

INDX guide · 1. Introduction · steps 1–14
INDX 1.1

How to navigate through the manual

↗
  • Use the graphical navigation buttons in the bottom right corner or the arrow keys on your keyboard:
  • Play backward button / Up arrow key - Moves to the previous step.
  • Left arrow button / Left arrow key - Moves to the previous image, or to the previous step if it’s the first image in the step.
  • Next button / Right arrow key - Moves to the next image, or to the next step if it’s the last image in the step.
  • Play forward (Next) button / Down arrow key - Moves to the next step.
  • Click on Contents to expand the full list of steps in this guide. This allows you to jump to any step regardless of the sequence.
  • Click on Comments to open the discussion for a specific step and leave your feedback.

View high resolution images

↗
  • When you browse the guide on help.prusa3d.com, you can view the original images in high resolution for clarity.
  • Just click on the image to open it in high resolution for a detailed view.
  • Click on Fullscreen mode or press the F key to maximize your screen space and focus entirely on the instructions.
INDX 1.3

Before you begin

↗
Compiler's noteYou don't need the companion article or the Gen 2 guide open: this document already follows the article's switching instructions. The original pages are linked from every step if you want to check them.
  • iIf you plan on installing the Prusa CORE One+ Gen 2 upgrade along with the Prusa INDX conversion, follow the instructions here: Conversion of the PRUSA INDX Core One to Gen 2
  • ✓The INDX Conversion kit is compatible with the Prusa CORE One and CORE One+. This guide uses the CORE One+; some disassembly steps may vary between models.
  • The required steps depend on your printer’s current state:
  • If your CORE One+ is brand new and still unboxed, first follow the CORE One+ Unpacking & First run guide  before installing the INDX conversion.
  • If you already use the CORE One+ and have purchased the INDX Conversion kit without the Gen 2 upgrade, you can continue with this guide.
  • !Do not discard any removed parts or fasteners until instructed. Some parts will be reused later in the upgrade.
  • iThis guide is for both the 4-tool and the 8-tool PRUSA Core One/+ INDX conversion kit.
  • Some photos may show the 8-tool version. This does not affect the conversion process for the 4-tool version.
2 comments online, none with practical info · read online
INDX 1.4

All the required tools are included

↗
  • Tools required for this upgrade:
  • ✓Use the tools originally included with your CORE One+ / CORE One printer.
  • Needle-nose pliers (1x)
  • Philips (PH2) screwdriver (1x)
  • Universal wrench (1x)
  • Allen key set
  • Torx key set
  • iThe T10 screwdriver is included only with kit versions and may not be available with fully assembled printers. 
    It is not required, but may be more convenient in some steps.
  • We also recommend printing out the community-made Snap-rivet-remover
2 useful comments of 4
langjai · 2026-09-24
Do yourself a favor and get yourself some good tools for this project. While you can get your work done with these tools, having the right tools will speed up the process and really limit your frustration. Some tools that I used were:

* Flush cutters (good for removing rivets too).
* T-handle metric socket set with ball end. I used Park Tool set, but any T-handle will do.
* Electronics driver kit. I used iFixit Mako Driver kit with 64 bits. It comes with a flexible extension that was REALLY useful for tight spaces.
* Electric screwdriver kit.
* ESD tweezers kit. Preferably one with a round tip.
* Head lamp
* A 5.5mm 6-point socket or a tiny flat plier to hold the M3 nuts.
* M3 tap
* An INDX-specific 3D-printed hardware bin.
* Nitrile gloves
* Prusa grease and linear motor grease kit (it's a good time to do some maintenance while you're at it).
* Tape measure
* Blue shop towels

Spare bag

INDX 1.7

Printed parts - versioning

↗
  • Most of the 3D printed parts are marked with their version.
  • E, F and Gx series (e.g. E1) - those parts are printed on Prusa Research farm and are distributed with the kit.
  • R, S and Tx series (e.g. R1) - those parts are available for download at https://www.printables.com/model/1758233-core-one-indx-printed-parts. They are identical to the factory ones.
  • The numbers indicate minor revisions that usually involve small design tweaks. A different label in the manual (e.g., a different version shown in photos) does not affect the assembly – all versions are fully compatible.
  • iif you have issues while assembling the printer with a specific printed part, find the label and share it with our support team.

INDX 1.9

Pro tip: inserting the nuts

↗
  • 3D printed parts are very precise, however, there still might be a tolerance in the printed part and the same goes for the size of the nut.
  • Therefore it might happen, that the nut won't fit easily in or might be falling out. Let's see, how to fix it:
  • Nut won't fit in: use a screw with a thread along its entire length (typically: M3x10, M3x18) and screw it from the opposite side of the opening. While tightening the screw, the nut will be pulled in. Remove the screw afterwards.
  • Nut keeps falling out: Use a piece of tape to fix the nut temporarily in place, as soon as you insert the screw in, you can remove the tape. Using glue isn't recommended as it can partly reach into the thread and you won't be able to tighten the screw properly.
  • Every time we recommend using the "screw pulling technique", you will be reminded with Joe's avatar ;)
  • iParts in the pictures are used as an example.
INDX 1.10

Electronics protection (ESD)

↗
  • !WARNING: Make sure to protect the electronics against electrostatic discharge (ESD). Always unpack the electronics right before you need them!
  • Here are some tips to prevent damage to the electronics:
  • Keep the electronics inside the ESD bag right until you are asked to install them.
  • Always touch the sides of the board only while handling it. Avoid touching the components on the surface.
  • Before you touch the electronics use any conductive (metal) structure nearby to neutralize the possible static charge from your hands.
  • Be extra cautious in rooms with carpets, which are often a source of electrostatic energy.
  • Clothes made of wool or certain synthetic fabrics can easily gather static electricity too. It is safer to wear cotton clothing for the assembly.

Jim · 2026-08-31
I'm not sure why they want us to follow the MMU3 build guide backwards. It's a fair amount of work to figure out what to do along side what NOT to do. I feel like they could have just added a page or two of steps for us to follow instead. Here's what I did for my MMU3 **Enclosed** version. It appears that the Lite version mounts differently (and more simply).

- Remove the top cover.
- Unload any existing filament from the MMU3.
- Power off and unplug the printer.
- Remove all of the PTFE tubes from the back of the MMU3 by pushing in the collet and pulling the tubes out.
- Remove the buffer assembly from the CORE One.
- Remove the PTFE tube from the Nextruder and the MMU3.
- On the back of the MMU3 you will see a data cable that runs down and connects to the back of the CORE One. Remove the cable from the MMU3 by pressing the release tab and pull the cable straight out. You will remove the other end of the cable when the INDX instructions have you open up the back of the case.
- Remove the MMU3. There are 4 Torx screws to remove. Two in the back are threaded into the case itself. Two (one on each side) are held in place with nyloc nuts, so you will need a wrench to hold the nut in place while you unscrew the Torx screw. Once the screws are removed, you can lift the MMU3 off of the case.

I'm quoting this from memory having just completed it. So take that into consideration while following these steps.

INDX 1.14

Prepare your desk

↗

  • Clear your workspace. Make sure you have enough room. A nice clear flat workbench will get you the results you are aiming for.

  • Let there be light! Make sure you are in a well-lit environment. Another lamp or even an extra flashlight will probably come in handy.

  • Prepare something to contain the plastic bags and the removed packing materials so you can recycle them afterwards. Make sure there are no important parts being discarded.

  • A minimum working space of 1.5 × 1.5 meters (60 × 60 inches) is recommended.
  • !We highly recommend placing a soft pad on your workbench. Some sheet metal parts have sharp edges that could scratch the surface.
  • iYou can use a piece of cardboard as a protective pad.
  • Let's start with chapter 2. Printer preparation & dissasembly.
INDX guide · 2. Printer preparation & disassembly · steps 1–36

B. Left side opened, rear bed spacer & offset sensorArticle · INDX 3.11–3.19

ARTICLE

Securing the bed spacer - right, additional information

↗

Follow the Prusa INDX guide from the start.

Keep following the instructions in the Prusa INDX guide until you finish step SECURING THE BED SPACER - RIGHT, then read the instructions below in this article:

Before you move on to the next step in the Prusa INDX guide, we need to disconnect the X and Y motor cables and remove the left side panel and cover from the printer to accommodate the GEN 2 upgrades.

Follow the instructions below:

  • Press the safety latch to disconnect the X and Y motor cables from the xBuddy board on the back of the printer.
  • Gently pull the X and Y motor cables slightly to create some slack while keeping the connectors inside the electronics compartment.

  • Remove all five nylon rivets securing the left top see-through side cover. Support the cover by hand when removing the last rivets to prevent it from falling.
  • Remove the side cover from the printer and set it aside in a safe, clean place.
  • Remove the eleven nylon rivets securing the left side metal panel. Support the panel by hand when removing the last rivets to prevent it from falling.
  • Remove the metal panel from the printer.

Once the motors are unplugged and the left panel and cover are removed, return to the Prusa INDX guide step REMOVING THE REAR BED SPACER, and continue from there.

  • You will notice that the left panel and side cover are still in place in the Prusa INDX conversion guide. Proceed as if the left side cover and panel were removed in the Prusa INDX guide.

Keep following the instructions in the Prusa INDX guide until you finish step SECURING THE OFFSET SENSOR CABLE.

As a correction, I threaded the screw myself with M3 thread. There was no spare part present in the supplied bag that I could fall back on.

I would advise checking this beforehand, as not everyone has the ability to cut threads themselves.
Otherwise, the update went well and everything worked properly right from the start. Test prints are currently being made to compare with the pre-update situation. The first results look good. The printer is also running much more quietly.

Regards,
Theo.

GEN 2 4.6

Installing the expansion joint screws

↗
  • Place the two PTFE washers on top of each other in the front threaded hole of the Z-carriage.
  • Insert the expansion joint screw through the washers into the threaded hole.
  • Tighten the screw fully, but do not overtighten.
  • iA small gap between the washers and the screw head is normal due to the screw's non-threaded section.
  • Proceed the same for the rest of the threaded holes.

E. Gen 2 belts & pulleysArticle · Gen 2 3.4–3.38

ARTICLE

Additional information and removing the belts

↗

Before you move on to the next step, we need to remove the right side panel and side cover from the printer to implement the GEN 2 upgrades.

Follow the instructions below:

  • Remove all five nylon rivets securing the right top see-through side cover. Support the cover by hand when removing the last rivet to prevent it from falling.
  • Remove the side cover from the printer and set it aside in a safe, clean place.
  • Remove the eleven nylon rivets securing the right steel side panel. Support the panel by hand when removing the last rivet to prevent it from falling.
  • Remove the metal panel from the printer.

With the right side panel and cover removed, read the information and instructions below in this article before proceeding:

In the following section, note the differences in photos and assembly process between the Prusa INDX conversion guide and the Gen 2 upgrade guide. These are listed below and do not affect the assembly process:

The PTFE tube leading to the filament sensor is removed in the Prusa INDX guide, but is visible in the GEN 2. guide.

The Bowden-guide is visible in the photos. It is also attached back onto the motor assembly in the GEN 2 guide. We will not need it for the Prusa CORE One INDX conversion process; you can remove it from the printer once it is detached from the motor mount.

Belt-tensioner screws:

During the upcoming belt exchange instructions in the GEN 2 guide, we recommend using the Prusa lubricant found in the Fasteners 2/2 bag in the Prusa CORE One/+ INDX conversion kit.

  • Apply a small amount of Prusa lubricant to the tip of both left and right M3x30 belt tensioning screws you removed earlier.
  • Spread the lubricant evenly around the entire thread and insert the screws back into the belt tensioner.
  • Skip this step when it later appears in the INDX guide.

With the above-mentioned information in mind, let's proceed with the Prusa CORE One+ GEN 2 upgrade and the Prusa CORE One/+ INDX conversion:

Switch to the GEN 2 guide step REMOVING THE BELTS, and continue from there.

Keep following the instructions in the GEN 2 guide until you finish step GUIDING THE UPPER BELT (GANTRY-RIGHT).

GEN 2 3.9

Installing the new pulley (right motor)

↗
Compiler's noteFrom comments: many people found the new pulleys very hard to push onto the motor shaft, here and on the left motor (Gen 2 3.22).
  • Rotate the motor shaft so that the flat faces you. Do not rotate the shaft any further.
  • Slide the new T21-1.5GT pulley onto the end of the shaft, with the set screw side facing the motor.
  • Insert the Pulley-offset-tool, with the side marked "Y", between the motor and the pulley to set the correct distance.
  • Press the pulley against the Pulley-offset-tool and tighten the set screw against the flat on the motor shaft.
  • Rotate the pulley and tighten the second set screw.

Mike G. · 2026-09-22
If you are upgrading an INDX machine, make sure that after the four screws are through the frame and into the motor, the motor/mount assembly is positioned as far forward (towards the front of the printer) as possible before tightening the 4 screws. There is a small amount of play in the location of the motor within the bent-metal frame and the indexing holes.

If you loosely assemble the motor/mounts without pushing them fully forward, you may run into dock calibration issues, like I did with tools 1–2 and 7–8.

Both motor/mount assemblies should be pushed as far forward as possible within the indexing holes before tightening everything down. This will help prevent dock calibration issues.

INDX 4.5

Installing the Gantry-aligner-tool - right

↗
  • Start by slightly loosening three screws on the back of the gantry on each side.
  • Place one of the Gantry-aligner-tool on the front right side of the X-axis, aligning the linear rail with the matching cutout.
  • iBoth Gantry-aligner-tools are identical.
  • The fork must face the pulleys.
  • Slide the Gantry-aligner-tool fully onto the gantry frame profile, ensuring the cutouts engage.
  • Route both free belt ends through the open space above the tool.
INDX 4.6

Installing the Gantry-aligner-tool - left

↗
  • Place the Gantry-aligner-tool on the front left side of the X-axis, aligning the linear rail with the matching cutout.
  • The fork must face the pulleys.
  • Slide the Gantry-aligner-tool fully onto the gantry frame profile, engaging the cutouts.
  • Route both free belt ends through the open space above the tool.
  • With each Gantry-aligner-tool in place, tighten the three screws on each side of the back of the gantry.

INDX 4.10

Securing the belts

↗
Compiler's noteGen 2 path: commenters found this one of the hardest steps with the new, finer-pitch belts. Many of them fully unscrewed the front belt tensioners first, attached both belt ends to the head-mounting plate, and then refitted the tensioners. Also check that plenty of teeth stick out (see comments). Don't overdo it, though: one commenter on INDX 4.11 had homing and calibration failures with the belt ends flush, until they moved each end about 1 mm back.
  • Hold the Head-mounting-plate in the correct orientation, using the protrusion as a guide.
  • From the right side, route the lower belt through the rear center opening in the Head-mounting-plate, around the post, and back out. It must extend 4–5 teeth.
  • Route the upper belt through the front center opening in the Head-mounting-plate, around the post, and back out. It must extend 4–5 teeth.
  • !Make sure the belts are not crossed.
  • Hold the right belts in place with your thumb to prevent them from slipping out.
  • Route the upper belt through the front center opening out (down) of the Head-mounting-plate. It must extend 6–7 teeth.
  • From the left side, route the lower belt through the rear center opening out (down) of the Head-mounting-plate. It must extend 6–7 teeth.
  • Insert the belt ends from the left side into the left opening and press them in. Leave 4–5 teeth protruding on from the rear side of the Head-mounting-plate.

Adjusting the belts

↗

G. Side covers, PTFE tubes, wiper, dock fan cableArticle · INDX 4.53–4.71, 5.1–5.17

ARTICLE

Mounting the side panels, PTFE and right cover

↗

Before you move on to the next step in the Prusa INDX guide, we need to attach both of the top see-through side panels.

Follow the instructions below:

  • Use four nylon rivets to reattach the left top see-through side cover. Do not insert a nylon rivet into the top middle hole. This is where we will mount the filament sensor in the Prusa INDX guide later.
  • Mount the right top see-through side cover. If you have the 8-tool version of the Prusa CORE One INDX, do not insert the top-middle nylon rivet as well.

With both top see-through covers mounted back, continue following the Prusa INDX guide step PTFE TUBES - LEFT SIDE: PARTS PREPARATION, and continue from there.

Keep following the instructions in the Prusa INDX guide until you finish step SECURING THE ZIP TIES II.

RedMedia · 2026-08-30
IMPORTANT, read this before proceeding.

I tried this part here, and after aligning joints, all of them turned away wrongly while tightening. Here's my suggestion for this step.

First, tighten all screws lightly, so the expansion joint can still move but the bed is already somewhat fixed and centered.
Skip ahead until you see the tightening order. Tighten the middle screw first, but completely. Then, proceed with the 4 middle ones the following way:

Put on the aligner tool up to the heatbed and turn it slightly counter-clockwise, so the joint is slightly off from the preferred rotation. Start tightening the screw and keep the joint actively from turning by holding it slightly turned. Finish tightening the screw either fully, or if the expansion joint didnt turn AT ALL, help turning it a bit by cancelling the counter rotation on the tool for the last millimeter of screw-tightening.
Loosen the tool up and slide it back on fully to verify that the joint has the correct orientation. If it doesn't, dont fully loosen the screw, just make slight adjustments with the tool and the torx screwdriver simultaneously. Verify again, skip to the next one.

For the one on the front right, I looked over the 45° edge of the board straight, so i couldn't see the face of the 45 edge anymore, looking perfectly over it. I now oriented that joint perfectly parallel to the edge, so it has the correct orientation as well.

I take no responsibility for what happens when you follow my guide, however, this is what worked best and fastest for me and I thought i'd share if someone has the same troubles.

Fixing the heatbed

↗
Compiler's noteThis is the last Gen 2 step for now. The article section that follows tightens the offset sensor, reconnects the X/Y motors and refits the left panel.

  • Center screw

I. Closing up, spool holders & tool dockArticle · INDX 5.18–5.104

ARTICLE

Mounting the left cover, covering the electronics

↗

Now that the expansion joints are aligned, let's return to the step we skipped in the Prusa INDX guide and secure the offset sensor assembly by tightening the M3x10 screw.

The screw forms its own thread in the plastic. Do not overtighten.

  • You will notice that the right-side cover is still in place in the photo above. Proceed as if it were not there; it does not affect the process.

Once the heatbed is secured and the expansion joints are aligned, we can connect the X and Y motor cables and mount the left-side cover.

Follow the instructions below:

  • Connect the left motor cable (X motor) to the left connector on the xBuddy board. It is labeled X.
  • Connect the right motor cable (Y motor) to the right connector on the xBuddy board. It is labeled Y.
  • Make sure that the safety latches click in place.

  • Mount the left side panel back onto the printer. Secure it in place with 3 nylon rivets in the highlighted positions.

Once the left side cover is secured in place with three nylon rivets, we are finished with the CORE One GEN 2 guide.

Return to the Prusa INDX guide to step ELECTRONICS COVERS: PARTS PREPARATION and follow the rest of the Prusa INDX guide to finish the conversion.

Installing the rear cover

↗

Compiler's noteDon't rely on the "bottom edge" wording in your PDF export of the INDX guide (generated 30 Sep 2026). For this step it says "Double-check that the nut is inserted in the same hole closer to the bottom edge, with the arrow pointing LEFT next to it." The web version of INDX 5.38 said the same about the bottom edge (arrow pointing DOWN) until Prusa changed it to "Double-check that the nuts are inserted as shown" in early October 2026. The photos didn't change. From comments: several people say the photos for this step and INDX 5.38 are swapped or misleading, and that the nut belongs in the hole closer to the top edge ("the up arrow side"). On INDX 5.38, others got it to work by flipping the tool. Whichever way you hold it, look through the holes to check that the nuts line up with the screw holes before you push the tool up.

INDX 5.46

Tilting the printer

↗
  • iPictured is the 8-tool version of the Prusa CORE One/+ INDX with bottom-right puck holders and the right filament sensors included.
  • Remove the Prusament box from the heatbed and place it behind the printer.
  • Move the toolhead to the back of the printer.
  • Place all the PTFE tubes inside the printer.
  • Place the box behind the printer and slowly and carefully lay the printer down so it can lean on the box.
  • !Ensure that the printer is stable and that it can not slide or fall when tilted. We recommend asking someone to hold the printer while it rests on the box to ensure your safety.
  • Ensure that the filament sensor cables are not pinched.

INDX 5.66

Assembling the tool holder

↗
  • Fully thread the M3x12cT screw into both holes of the Tool-holder, then remove the screw.
  • iThis creates a thread in the part, making the Tool-holder easier to install on the front profile later.
  • Position the Tool-holder with the countersunk holes facing up.
  • Insert each Thimble into the oval hole in part Tool-holder.
  • Insert a large spring (0.5 x 8.5 x 30 x 15) into each Thimble.
  • Insert two small springs (0.63 x 5 x 15 x 11) into the side holes of part Tool-holder.
  • Repeat the same procedure for all remaining Tool-holder parts.

INDX 5.67

Installing the tool holders

↗
  • In the correct orientation, place the Tool-holder against position 1 on the underside of the front profile.
  • Align the holes in both parts.
  • !CAUTION: When placing the Tool-holder, make sure no spring is pinched against the front profile.
  • Secure the Tool-holder using two M3x12cT screws.
  • iThe screw forms its own thread in the plastic. Slight resistance is expected.
  • Grasp the Tool-holder and gently wiggle it. It must not be rigid - a slight, barely perceptible looseness is required.
  • ✓Repeat the procedure for the remaining Tool-holder assemblies on the front profile, ideally in order 1–4, then 8–5 for easier handling.

HChar · 2026-09-11
If you want the same LED strip position as with C1+ non-INDX variant has, without printing any holders, now would be a good time to install the strip to the back side of the gantry (behind the screw holes where the green arrows are pointing).

How to (A and B):
A: See first comment in the 89.
B (how I did it):
Avoid touching LEDs and resistors
1. Remove the LED panel.
2. Slowly and carefully remove the LED strip from the LED panel, avoid over 90° angles when removing the strip, it should come off quite easily.
3. Reinsert the strip to the new location shown in the first picture with green arrows.
4. LED strip should be fully hidden when viewing from the front.

INDX tools only slightly limit the lights, but added bonus is that you are able to see the nozzles much better if they are dirty or have any markings on them after printing.

  • The printer will now prompt you to fine-tune the belts. Follow the on-screen instructions.

  • Adjusting belt tension (CORE One)
  • The belts are adjusted using the tensioning mechanism on each side for each belt:
  • The left screw adjusts the upper belt.
  • The right screw adjusts the lower belt.

What to do if gaps exist?
krisztian96 · 2026-09-01
Quick gantry alignment
If there is a gap on either side of the gantry, you can try to force it in the opposite direction manually:

1. Fully loosen both tensioner bolts; this will allow free gantry movement.
2. Move the gantry halfway back along the rails.
3. Grip the gantry firmly on both ends and apply a gentle counter-force in the opposite direction of the tilt until it straightens.
4. Check the alignment with the belts still loose, and carefully push the gantry forward. Since the loose belts will not pull it all the way, you may need to guide it by hand. Verify that there is no gap on either side at the front position.
5. Tighten both tensioner bolts gradually, alternating between them, tightening each by the same amount to keep the gantry straight. You may hold the gantry in place with your hand while tightening. After tightening both belts, make sure no gap has reappeared.

Note: Apply force carefully to avoid damaging belts or bearings.
